elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered grant: "Kubient hereby grants to Customer and, upon written notice to Kubient, its affiliates a limited, royalty-free... license". "Customer" is defined as The Associated Press alone, so the added words supply genuinely new affiliate coverage (no duplication).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No reference to contractors, service providers, or persons acting on Customer's behalf appears in the rendered grant; the clause also retains "without right of sublicense", which would block contractor use. To meet this element the grant must read e.g. "...and contractors acting on Customer's behalf".

The grant contains no term language making it perpetual; it remains a royalty-free licence coterminous with the Services and subject to revocation (paragraph 4(c)(ii) revokes the licence on termination).

The word "revocable" is expressly retained in the rendered clause ("without right of sublicense, revocable license"). The deterministic check "no at-will revocation remains" reports ok, but on the face of the operative text at-will revocability survives; the check should not be relied on for this element.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No breach-limited termination standard was inserted; the licence remains revocable and paragraph 4(c)(ii)'s revocation mechanic is untouched.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The insertion is narrower than the preferred element: "transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition" only. Successors by consolidation, reorganisation, or operation of law outside an M&A transaction are not covered; the preferred wording requires unqualified successor transferability.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "grants to Customer and, upon written notice to Kubient, its affiliates" — the affiliate extension is expressly conditioned on written notice to Vendor, matching the fallback trigger exactly.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "revocable license, transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition"; the previously blocking words "non-transferable, non-assignable" were deleted, so no retained sentence contradicts the new permission.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language (affiliate coverage on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor), not merely promised in the margin comment.

Preferred is not complete: contractor coverage, perpetuity, irrevocability, and the breach-only termination standard are all absent, and the successor-transfer wording is narrowed to M&A. The drafter's decision to sit at fallback is consistent with the rendered text.

Note on deterministic evidence: the "no at-will revocation remains" check returns ok, but the clause still reads "revocable license". That is immaterial to the fallback checklist (which does not require irrevocability) and does not trigger walk-away, because affiliates now have an express path to coverage — walk-away requires revocability plus no affiliate/contractor path.

Minimality holds: the only deletions are "non-transferable, non-assignable", which directly contradict the selected transfer element and had to go to avoid an internally inconsistent clause. Customer-favourable restrictions outside the checklist ("limited", "non-exclusive", "without right of sublicense", "revocable", the purpose limitation) are all retained, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, personnel/access language) were added. No duplicate affiliate coverage arises because the defined "Customer" is The Associated Press alone.

Intent is preserved: royalty-free scope, the Target Demand purpose limitation, the Google Ad Manager sentence, and the paragraph 4(c)(ii) revocation mechanic all survive without contradiction. The licence-level transfer permission is a direct permission rather than a broad "notwithstanding" override of the paragraph 14(h) assignment clause, so no cross-reference conflict is created. (The pre-existing mismatch in 4(c)(ii) referring to "the license granted under section 3" and the empty defined-term parenthetical are legacy artefacts, not introduced by this edit.)

If the team later wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are: delete "revocable", add "and contractors acting on Customer's behalf", state that the licence is perpetual and irrevocable once paid up (or terminable only for uncured material breach), broaden "successor by merger or acquisition" to "successors", and conform paragraph 4(c)(ii).
